thread:
jon: quick note — trying to reconcile a weird perf delta between synthetic load and replay harness results for the new kernel-gating heuristic. can folks who ran the replay experiments paste logs? :eyes:

maria: saw this earlier. synthetic p95 looks great (~120ms), replay p95 jumps to ~380ms for the same qps. suspect KV cache warming + kernel selection path divergence.

sasha: confirmed. replay traces show a lot more small-batch kernel fallbacks when KV miss rate is high. that increases per-token latency.

alex: what are the KV hit rates in the two runs? synthetic primes prefixes, replay has many cold keys. numbers?

maria: synthetic run KV hit ~94% after priming. replay run hit ~48% at t=0, slowly climbs to ~75% over 6m.

jon: that explains it. kernel-gating currently uses sequence-level heuristics that prefer fused attention when batch shapes are large and prefix present. with high miss-rate we get fragmented batches and fallback to generic kernel.

sasha: reproducer attached earlier (see /replay-run-042). replay-bot: rerun 042 with --warmup=enabled shows dramatic improvement.

replay-bot: rerun complete. summary:
- baseline replay (no warmup): p95=382ms, p99=520ms, kv_hit_start=49%
- replay + warmup: p95=142ms, p99=210ms, kv_hit_start=91%

ci-bot: note: kernel selection logs for the warmup run show 82% of steps used optimized fused kernel v2, previous run only 21% used fused v2.

ops: autoscale notes — when we pushed QPS up to 2k the Dedicated pool consumed burst credits for ~3m then scaled up 1 extra node after ~24s, but GPUs took ~40s to accept traffic (driver init). overall scale-up from 0->ready ~64s.

alex: can we get apples-to-apples? i.e., synthetic run that reproduces the same cold KV distribution and batch shapes as the replay. otherwise we can be misled.

maria: created a synthetic generator that stochastically mirrors replay prefix lengths and key reuse. running now with kernel-gating toggled on/off.

jon: early numbers from that generator: with realistic KV miss distribution and no warmup, synthetic p95 ~360ms (close to replay). enabling warmup reduces to ~150ms. so warmup is doing the heavy lifting.

sasha: interesting thread: kernel-gating interacts with batching heuristics. when gating is aggressive it waits slightly longer to form large batches (adds ~2-3ms tail) but that gives fused kernels a big win. with fragmented batches the gating causes fallbacks and worse p99.

alex: profiling snapshot (hot path):
```
CPU: scheduling + memcopy 6ms
GPU kernel launch overhead 1ms
fused-attn kernel exec 18ms
generic-attn kernel exec 42ms
KV lookup + priming (miss path) 35ms
```

jon: actionable: 1) treat warmup priming as first-class in autoscale lifecycle (pre-warm KV on new nodes), 2) add a short preflight traffic spike to consume burst credits for Dedicated so GPUs are ready, 3) tweak gating threshold to be less aggressive under high miss rates.

maria: also propose a small change to the replay harness: capture exact batch-shape timeline and replay that as a synthetic trace (ensures deterministic apples-to-apples).

ops: for Dedicated pools we can add a small always-on warmup lane (1-2% capacity) that keeps KV cache warmed for new arrivals. tradeoff: steady-state cost vs lower p99 on scale-up.

sasha: open question: how long to keep warm lane? bursts of 5-10m common — maybe keep for 10m after last heavy traffic. need telemetry to tune.

jon: PRs inbound: gating-threshold-tweak, prewarm-on-scale, replay-harness-batch-trace. will tag reviewers.

maria: recorded a short demo clip of the replay vs synthetic generator comparison — uploading to the thread. :thumbsup:

alex: small follow-up experiment request: run the tuner with quantized fused kernel path disabled to measure pure batching impact (no kernel advantage) — to isolate batching heuristics impact vs kernel speedups.

jon: agreed. i'll queue that. final: next sync tomorrow 11am to review numbers and decide warm-lane/always-on policy.

ops: FYI we have 2 incident reports that mention slow p99 after scale events — i'll link them in the follow-up so PLs can correlate.

maria: thanks all. seems like warmup + smarter autoscale preflight will close most of the gap.

sasha: tl;dr: apples-to-apples requires matching KV distribution + batch shapes; warmup is the biggest single lever; kernel selection amplifies wins if batching shapes are favorable. :white_check_mark:
